name: InMode Evolve

lead: InMode Evolve is a clinic treatment for body contouring. Applicators sit on the area while the machine runs, so there is no surgery, needles or manual work.
People use it to look more toned and defined around the abdomen, flanks, thighs and arms, usually across a short series of visits.

paras: The system is marketed as using radiofrequency energy to warm the skin and fat layer and electrical muscle stimulation to contract the muscle underneath, aiming at a firmer, more defined contour.

Temporary redness, warmth and muscle soreness are the commonly described effects of this kind of treatment. It is operated by licensed providers, and people with implanted electronics or certain conditions are usually advised to check first.

angle.text: People book Evolve sessions to sharpen the look of the midsection, thighs or arms without surgery. Because the applicators work hands-free, a session involves lying still while the device runs, and treatments are generally repeated over several visits.

lead: InMode Evolve is a hands-free body-contouring platform made by the aesthetics-device company InMode. Clinics offer it as a way to refine the shape of the abdomen, flanks, thighs, arms and buttocks without surgery or needles, with applicators strapped or placed on the area while the patient rests.

People use it to look leaner and more defined: the system is marketed as combining radiofrequency heating of the skin and fat layer with muscle stimulation, aiming at a tighter, more sculpted silhouette. Sessions are typically booked as a short series at a clinic or medspa.

The Evolve System has been cleared by the US FDA through the 510(k) pathway in more than one configuration: the Tone applicator (K201285, decision March 5, 2021, classified as a powered muscle stimulator) and the Transform applicator (K231495, decision October 13, 2023).[1][2] A single-group InMode-sponsored study registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, linked from the Transform record, measured abdominal circumference change at three months.[2]
infobox: Tone applicator K201285 (2021); Transform applicator K231495 (2023)[1][2]

paras: Evolve is part of InMode's line of non-surgical body platforms and is delivered by trained providers. The hands-free design means applicators are fixed in place, so one operator can treat several areas in a session. The platform is offered with different applicators for different goals, with the Tone version classified by the FDA as a powered muscle stimulator (Class II) and the Transform version recorded under an electrosurgical product code.[1][2]

The FDA database records the Evolve System with the Tone Applicator as cleared on March 5, 2021 through the traditional 510(k) pathway, with product code IPF.[1] The Evolve System with the Transform Applicator was cleared on October 13, 2023.[2] A 510(k) clearance reflects a finding of substantial equivalence to a legally marketed device.

Within appearance-focused communities, devices like Evolve are discussed as a non-surgical option for tightening and defining the body after weight loss, or for areas that diet and training leave less defined. Costs vary by clinic and by the number of sessions.

Energy-based body treatments are performed by licensed providers. Commonly reported effects of radiofrequency and muscle-stimulation treatments in general include temporary redness, warmth and muscle soreness; individuals with implanted electronic devices or certain medical conditions are usually advised to check with their provider first.

A registered study (NCT05398159) listed on the Transform clearance record is described as a single-group, open-label, industry-sponsored study of 75 patients at five sites, started in March 2021, with change in abdominal circumference by tape measure at three months as the primary outcome and blinded photo identification as a secondary outcome. Its title refers to a related InMode product, and published results were not found.[2]

timeline.event: FDA clears the Evolve System with the Tone Applicator (K201285).[1]
FDA clears the Evolve System with the Transform Applicator (K231495).[2]
